messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT #4321 — 2026-03-11 09:03Z — elevated 5xx rate across hosted inference region us-west-2. Potential memory regressions observed in model-serving nodes. Paging eng-oncall.
elaine: got it, I'm oncall. seeing a sustained 12% 5xx for text-generation endpoints, tail latency spikes to ~2.4s. rolling 5m window shows error source from model-runtime replicas (OOM in logs).
sam: tagging in. can you attach the pod logs + node mem stats? are we failing forward or rejecting?
elaine: attaching brief snippet:```kube logs model-runner-57f8 | tail -n 50
2026-03-11T09:02:14Z ERROR runtime: alloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-11T09:02:14Z WARN attempt to restart container
```
michael: support team seeing ~30 customer requests impacted (varied SLAs). Most are short chat gen calls — customers getting 500 with body: "runtime error: insufficient memory". I've flagged highest-revenue tenants and paused non-critical background batch jobs for them.
jess: product-ops: halting new canary traffic and switching routing policy to lower-memory variants if available. Sam, do we have compatible quantized model variants to fallback to?
sam: yes — we have quantized v1.3 and v1.2-light that use ~30% less GPU memory. I'll push a routing rule to prefer v1.2-light for the next 30m as a mitigation. doing a canary swap to 10% first.
elaine: canary at 10% running now. initial success: no OOMs in that sample. increasing to 40% then 100% if stable.
ranjeet: support-bot — please create an incident channel entry for postmortem scheduling and customer comms. Include impacted tenants list and the mitigation steps taken.
support-bot: Created ticket INC-4321-postmortem in #incidents and draft status page update at https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/4321-draft.
michael: I'm drafting an outbound note for impacted customers. Plan: immediate status page update saying we mitigated via routing to memory-optimized model variants, full RCA and timeline promised in 72 hours, and offer to review logs with top impacted customers. Thoughts?
jess: agree. emphasize temporary routing decision and that model behavior will be fixed in the runtime, not changes to customer code. add a note about credits for affected tenants who hit SLOs.
sam: quick technical note for the postmortem: suspected regression in memory allocator introduced in runtime commit ce3a9f2 deployed 03/10 22:18 UTC. Action items during incident: rollback that commit on non-dedicated pools, patch allocator to avoid spike, and add mem-guard to prevent single-request growth beyond limit.
elaine: logging action items inline so we don't lose them: - Action: rollback ce3a9f2 on hosted pool (owner: sam) - Action: create mem-guard throttle in runtime (owner: sam) - Action: add alert for sudden memory-growth per replica (owner: elaine) - Action: customer communication + credits (owner: michael) - Action: schedule postmortem and invite SRE, Runtime, Product, Support (owner: jess)
ranjeet: can we get a postmortem meeting in the next 48 hours? I have availability: 03/12 16:00 UTC or 03/12 22:00 UTC. Need to include customer-facing ops too.
michael: 03/12 16:00 UTC works for me. Will share a calendar invite + pre-read draft.
jess: booked 03/12 16:00 UTC, sending invites now. Pre-read should include timeline, raw metrics, and the initial mitigation script we ran.
sam: rollback completed at 09:30Z — monitoring shows 5xx rate dropping to baseline. rolling back introduced minimal performance variance. Will open a PR with allocator patch and mem-guard unit tests.
elaine: monitoring stable, no further OOMs in last 20m. Reopening routing to standard variants gradually.
michael: status page updated: short note published and customers with significant impact emailed. Draft of full RCA in progress — target share to customers 03/14 09:00 UTC.
jess: for customer trust restoration, recommend: 1) transparent timeline + evidence (metrics screenshots), 2) concrete remediation plan with dates, 3) offer a 1:1 session for enterprise customers, 4) goodwill credits for SLO misses. I'll prepare a customer comms template.
sam: tracking remediation tasks in INC-4321 board. ETA for runtime fix: PR in review today, deploy patch to canary 03/12 morning, full rollout after postmortem validation.
ranjeet: support asked for a short FAQ to include in the status page — "Why did this happen?" "Is my data safe?" "Will this recur?" Michael, Jess: please handle.
michael: will add FAQ: confirm no data exfiltration, issue limited to memory allocation and not model weights or data. Will note steps taken to prevent recurrence.
elaine: thanks team. I'll hand off oncall to night squad at 18:00Z with notes here. If any customer escalations come in overnight, ping me and I'll brief the incoming oncall.
ranjeet: follow-up checklist for postmortem thread: - Confirm root cause and contributing factors - Capture timeline and decision points - Map action items to owners + due dates - Draft customer-facing RCA and legal review if needed - Close loop with impacted customers (1:1s)
jess: adding owners/dates: rollback done (sam, done), allocator PR (sam, 2026-03-12), mem-guard tests (sam, 2026-03-13), alerting (elaine, 2026-03-12), customer RCA draft (michael, 2026-03-14), customer meetings (michael, ongoing).
support-bot: Reminder scheduled: postmortem pre-read due 2026-03-12 12:00 UTC.
michael: final note — for trust restoration, propose a short webinar for enterprise customers where runtime and product explain the fix and mitigations. Jess: can you coordinate?
jess: will do. creating calendar and draft slides after postmortem.
elaine: handing off to night team now. last status: system stable, mitigation in place, postmortem scheduled. closing active paging.
incident-bot: INCIDENT #4321 status: mitigated. Postmortem scheduled. Follow-ups tracked in INC-4321.
